title: End-of-day reconciliation cannot read its positions input
telemetry: Supplied sanitized Cloud Storage console bucket and object details, Cloud Logging policy-denied audit log results, Cloud Run job execution history and application-owner reader records. The candidate receives static console observations and has no shell, cloud CLI, console session or bucket access. No restore, re-publish, perimeter or IAM change is part of the task.
owner: Oakley, Reconciliation on-call, owns the investigation. Sutton, the eod-recon-loader application owner, owns the reader job, its manifest handling and its client records; Ottilie, the positions data owner, owns bucket synthetic-eod-positions-drop, the positions publisher, its manifests and any restore or re-publish; Hollis, the security policy owner, owns the VPC Service Controls perimeter perimeter-custody-data and its ingress rules. ITO coordinates the existing TLC and change approvals.
task: Oakley has asked you to investigate why this morning's end-of-day reconciliation could not read its input from bucket synthetic-eod-positions-drop in synthetic-positions-prod, us-east4. Review the supplied console observations for 2026-10-15 05:30-06:20 UTC and return a bounded technical update for the existing TLC: the failure mechanism the records support, its evidence, remaining unknowns, and the next useful check with its owner. No change is approved.

sources.claim: Each object version has a generation number that identifies it. With Object Versioning enabled a replaced live version becomes noncurrent and keeps its generation; with it disabled the replaced live version is deleted, or soft-deleted when soft delete is enabled. The page does not state the error returned for a request naming an unavailable generation, so the fixture's 404 wording is an authored observation and is not graded; the case rests on the manifest and live-generation metadata.

Soft delete retains deleted or overwritten objects in a soft-deleted state for the retention duration (default 7 days, settable 7-90); soft-deleted objects cannot be read, modified or overwritten, only listed and restored. Whether a particular generation is retained therefore needs the owner's soft-deleted listing; the page does not list restore permissions, and the case assigns any restore to the data owner.

The generation parameter selects a specific revision instead of the latest version; softDeleted=true requires a generation and returns metadata only. The page does not document the not-found response for a missing generation.

A Cloud Storage request blocked by VPC Service Controls returns HTTP 403 with JSON error reason vpcServiceControls ('Request violates VPC Service Controls.'); the audit log is the primary debugging tool, denials are written to the protected project's cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fpolicy log with status code 7, and NO_MATCHING_ACCESS_LEVEL means the caller matched no access level or ingress rule. An IAM failure can look similar, and the page treats IAM and VPC Service Controls as separate checks.

Policy Denied audit logs cannot be disabled; entries carry violationReason, vpcServiceControlsUniqueId, securityPolicyInfo (the perimeter), dryRun (true only for dry-run checks), methodName and authenticationInfo.principalEmail, and sample queries use resource type audited_resource. The exact methodName string for a Cloud Storage read is not quoted, so the fixture describes it rather than grading it.

gcs_bucket identifies a bucket with project_id, bucket_name and location labels. The policy-denied entries and reader client records in this fixture are supplied console observations, not claimed native gcs_bucket log fields.

a.conclusion: VPC Service Controls perimeter perimeter-custody-data, enforced by CHG-5512 at 05:40 UTC, denies recon-loader's reads from synthetic-recon-prod: the reader's first read, the manifest, returned 403 with reason vpcServiceControls, and each attempt matches an enforced (dryRun=false) policy-denied entry with NO_MATCHING_ACCESS_LEVEL for that perimeter. Bucket IAM still grants the reader object read and the manifest names the live generation, so a missing IAM grant, a stale generation or lost data is not supported. Whether the perimeter was meant to admit this reader is unknown.
next_checks: Hollis compares perimeter-custody-data's ingress rules and access levels before and after CHG-5512 with recon-loader's documented access path and decides, through ITO's change approval, whether a scoped ingress rule for that identity and Cloud Storage reads is intended.

Oakley shares the reader-side 403 records and the four policy-denied entries, referencing their unique IDs, through the existing TLC and tracks the 08:00 UTC reconciliation need-by time with the operations desk.
After any approved perimeter change, Sutton confirms that the next eod-recon-loader execution reads the manifest and its named generation before anyone declares recovery.
unsupported: Adding IAM bindings or broad grants such as roles/storage.admin or allUsers access, when IAM already grants object read and is not the denying layer.
Removing synthetic-positions-prod from the perimeter, switching it to dry-run mode, or rolling back CHG-5512 without the security policy owner and change approval.
Blaming the 05:52 correction re-publish or a stale generation, or claiming the positions file was lost or must be restored or re-published.
Claiming to have queried logs, tested access or changed anything; the candidate only reviewed supplied observations.
unknowns: Whether CHG-5512 intended to admit recon-loader through an ingress rule or access level, and what rule set it applied.
Whether other readers outside the perimeter are affected, and any state after the 06:16 UTC capture.

b.conclusion: The reader requests generation 1792042267418223 named by the 05:31 manifest, but the 05:52 correction re-publish replaced that object with generation 1792043561906114 and did not rewrite the manifest; with Object Versioning disabled the earlier generation is no longer a readable version, so the request no longer matches the available object. The manifest read succeeded, and the policy-denied search shows no reader entry while it does return another principal's denial, so a perimeter or IAM denial is not supported. Whether the earlier generation is retained as soft-deleted, and which generation reconciliation should use, are unknown; neither data loss nor recoverability is established.
next_checks: Ottilie confirms which generation of positions/2026-10-14/eod-positions.csv is authoritative for the 2026-10-14 reconciliation and why the correction re-publish did not rewrite manifests/2026-10-14.json.

Ottilie reviews the bucket's soft-deleted listing for generation 1792042267418223 before anyone reports data loss or proposes a restore; any restore, manifest rewrite or re-publish is Ottilie's decision under ITO's change approval.

Sutton and Ottilie agree whether and when to rerun eod-recon-loader against a corrected manifest; Oakley tracks the 08:00 UTC need-by time in the existing TLC and confirms a successful read before declaring recovery.
unsupported: Blaming the 05:40 perimeter change, or rolling back CHG-5512 or changing ingress rules.
Declaring the positions data lost, or restoring the soft-deleted generation, overwriting the live object or rewriting the manifest without the data owner.
Changing the reader to take the latest live generation as the fix before the data owner decides which file is authoritative.
Granting broader bucket access or new IAM bindings, when the reader's manifest read succeeded under the existing grant.
unknowns: Which generation is authoritative for the 2026-10-14 reconciliation and why the manifest was not rewritten.
Whether generation 1792042267418223 is retained as soft-deleted within the 7-day retention, and any state after the 06:16 UTC capture.
